problem: Negative and float amounts are no longer rejected, so allocate('-10',[1,1]) returns negative shares and floats are accepted via str(), where main raised ValueError/TypeError.
int(amount.scaleb(places)) silently truncates excess decimals, so allocate('10.005',[1,1]) returns shares summing to 10.00 where main raised ValueError.
Weight validation is removed, so empty weights return [] (the whole amount is dropped) and zero or negative weights are accepted, e.g. [1,-1] returns [100.01,-99.99].
'sum(ws) or Fraction(1)' masks a zero total weight, so allocate('100',[0,0]) returns [0.01,0.01] and the shares no longer sum to the amount.
'max(leftover, 0)' clamps a negative leftover and hides a broken sum invariant instead of failing.
'places' is unvalidated, so places=-1 returns '1E+1' style values, bool is accepted, and a float raises a raw TypeError.
Non-finite and invalid inputs (NaN, Infinity, True) now raise inconsistent ValueError, OverflowError or InvalidOperation instead of a controlled ValueError/TypeError.
A behavioral rewrite of money-handling code ships with no tests pinning the removed validation or the largest-remainder tie-break.
_to_decimal is now dead code, which is why the float/bool type gate no longer applies.
The comment documenting tie-breaking by lowest index (stable sort) was deleted.
